subject.title: [Feature]: Batch WhatsApp messages by messageTimestamp instead of receive time

question: Should WhatsApp gain an opt-in multi-second timestamp-coalescing mode, and what exact hold duration, eligible message types, and flush boundaries define one logical user action?
rationale: The observable gap is real, but source inspection cannot choose the acceptable latency or safely disambiguate second-resolution timestamps; those choices establish a new public turn-boundary contract.

options.title: Opt-in bounded coalescing
options.body: Preserve current defaults and add a WhatsApp-only mode with a documented maximum hold plus strict sender, conversation, message-type, and flush invariants.

options.title: Require a stronger signal
options.body: Do not group by timestamp until Baileys exposes protocol grouping or composition metadata that avoids same-second ambiguity.

options.title: Change the default behavior
options.body: Enable timestamp-aware multi-second holding for all WhatsApp users and intentionally accept upgrade-visible latency and grouping changes.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded coalescing
recommendation.body: Preserve current defaults and add a WhatsApp-only mode with a documented maximum hold plus strict sender, conversation, message-type, and flush invariants.
